text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Pre-expedition medical: history, examination, resting ECG, kidney function and electrolytes, HbA1c, lipid panel, urine albumin, TSH, ALT, blood count, and baseline blood lead, vitamin C and vitamin D; audiogram; tuberculosis blood test because of a past household contact
  • Wilderness and expedition medicine consultation to advise on fitness for the command, treatment for years away from care, nutrition and food safety, cold injury, and evacuation
  • Blood pressure: a validated upper-arm home monitor with a large cuff, two readings morning and evening for seven days, to confirm the diagnosis; less salt, less alcohol, more vegetables and daily walking from today
  • Treatment: amlodipine 5 mg daily, with a goal below 130/80 mmHg at home, home readings weekly on board, and a supply for three years in blister packs; no diuretic or renin-angiotensin blocker because of dehydration, cold diuresis and no laboratory access; statin not started by his choice after a risk discussion
  • Heart before a strenuous remote posting: echocardiogram for stage 2 hypertension, and a symptom-limited exercise treadmill test once he has recovered from any acute illness
  • Weight: his own goals for walking, hill work, portions and alcohol, discussed without blame; no weight-loss medicine before departure
  • Nutrition and food safety for years without fresh food: vitamin C 250 mg daily in sealed, cool, dark storage, with food sources and a check of the expedition's stores; vitamin D3 daily; an energy-dense ration; canned food from suppliers without lead solder, inspected for bulging, leaking or damaged cans, which are discarded unopened; no home-canned food; a blood lead baseline
  • Cold: layered clothing with vapor control, dry socks and mitts, buddy checks of face, hands and feet, no tobacco or alcohol before cold exposure, rewarming of frostbite only when refreezing can be prevented, and hypothermia recognition and insulation in the field
  • Vaccinations, dental examination and treatment, and colorectal and other screening at the preventive visit before departure
  • Mind and isolation: baseline PHQ-9 and GAD-7, a routine of work, light, exercise and sleep through the polar night, a peer-support plan among the officers, and an evacuation plan with a medical kit, written instructions for the ship's surgeons, and a 12-month review of medicines
  • Hearing: audiogram, hearing protection around guns and engines, and seating so that his better ear faces the speaker

resource.title: Sir John Franklin synthetic care plan
resource.description: Fitness assessment of an older man before a multi-year Arctic expedition, with high blood pressure and obesity found at the pre-expedition medical: a 58-year-old naval officer chosen to command an expedition that will be years beyond the reach of hospital care. The episode covers confirming the diagnosis with home readings and treating stage 2 hypertension under the 2025 AHA/ACC guideline, choosing a medicine that needs no laboratory monitoring and suits dehydration and cold; cardiovascular risk with ECG, lipids, HbA1c, kidney function, urine albumin, echocardiography and an exercise treadmill test, and the PREVENT and Pooled Cohort risk estimates; weight managed by his own goals and without stigma; vitamin C and vitamin D and nutrition planning for years without fresh food; food safety, with canned-food quality, lead and botulism as modern risks; cold injury and hypothermia prevention under the Wilderness Medical Society guidelines; vaccinations, including rabies pre-exposure prophylaxis; dental care before departure; noise-induced hearing loss; mental health in isolation and polar darkness; a medical kit and an evacuation plan; and influenza in the weeks before departure, with oseltamivir and decongestant avoidance.
